items.text: Leaving Egypt and living in the promised land were steps toward God’s ultimate goal: that His people become holy, just as He is holy. Through covenants, laws, and sacrifices, the Israelites were taught about the Savior, the true path to holiness for them and for us.

The tabernacle was a place of holiness built by the Israelites to help them become a holy people through sacred ordinances. The items within the tabernacle, like the Ark of the Covenant and the altar of sacrifice, were meant to turn their thoughts and lives toward the Savior.

The Ark of the Covenant, a sacred object in the tabernacle, represents God’s presence and His covenant with His people. It reminds us that God dwells with those who keep His commandments and strive for holiness, pointing us to the Savior’s enduring promises.

The altar of incense, used for offerings, symbolizes the prayers of the saints ascending to God. It teaches us that our sincere prayers, offered in faith through the Savior, are precious to Him and are a vital part of our journey toward becoming holy.

The candlestick or lampstand in the tabernacle represents Jesus Christ, the Light of the World. As we follow Him, we are also called to be lights to others, illuminating the path of truth and righteousness, and helping them find their way to holiness.

The altar of sacrifice in the tabernacle foreshadowed the ultimate sacrifice of Jesus Christ. It taught the Israelites about atonement for sins and the need for repentance. This altar directs our hearts to the Savior’s infinite love and atoning power.

The laver, or basin of water, in the tabernacle symbolized cleansing and purification. It reminds us that through baptism and the Atonement of Jesus Christ, we can be washed clean from sin and made pure, preparing us to enter into holy places.

Leviticus 19 outlines laws given to the Israelites to help them increase in holiness. These commandments guide our actions and change our hearts, teaching us to seek holiness from the Lord and to live principles that draw us closer to Him.

The Lord asks us to offer our contributions to His work with a willing heart. Just as the Israelites gave willingly of their precious materials for the tabernacle, we are asked to offer our time, talents, and hearts, moved by the Spirit to serve.

Jesus Christ is able to make us holy. Like the Israelites leaving captivity, we can leave sin behind and follow Him. He has promised to cleanse us, to guide us, and to help us become more like Him through His Atoning sacrifice.
items.attribution: Doctrine and Covenants 60:7; Come, Follow Me—Old Testament 2026
